questions.prompt: Which statement best defines a production agent in this course?

options.text: A model with a long system prompt and several tools
A probabilistic decision component surrounded by deterministic control, trusted boundaries, durable state, and operations
Any chatbot that can call an API
A multi-agent team with named roles

questions.explanation: The model is one component. The application owns validation, authorization, persistence, effects, observation, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Which requirements directly imply a durable workflow?

options.text: A case may wait 30 days for a document
The landing page needs a light theme
A human approval may arrive after a deployment
The model should use structured output

questions.explanation: Long waits and late external signals require persisted execution state. Structured output is important but does not by itself require a durable workflow.

questions.prompt: What should an engineer do first when given 'build an onboarding agent'?

options.text: Select an agent framework
Choose the largest model
Define the user outcome, authority, risk, constraints, and non-goals
Create a vector database

questions.explanation: Architecture follows the user outcome and consequence of failure, not a preferred framework.

questions.prompt: Which use case most strongly justifies a bounded agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Apply a known tax rate to an invoice
Research an ambiguous entity across changing sources and decide which evidence gap to investigate next
Validate a JSON schema
Sort records by timestamp

questions.explanation: Dynamic action selection under uncertainty is a good reason for bounded autonomy. Deterministic rules should remain deterministic code.

questions.prompt: Which factors should reduce the amount of autonomy granted?

options.text: High consequence of a wrong action
Irreversible or hard-to-reconcile effects
Clear deterministic rules
A desire to use more agents in the diagram

questions.explanation: High consequence, irreversible effects, and clear deterministic logic all favor stronger workflow or human control.

questions.prompt: What is the best initial Atlas design?

options.text: Six autonomous specialist agents with unrestricted tools
A deterministic workflow with one bounded research loop where adaptivity adds value
One model prompt that performs the entire case
A human-only process with no measurement

questions.explanation: Start with the minimum autonomy that produces measurable benefit and expand only after evaluation.

questions.prompt: After a model returns a proposed tool call, what should happen next?

options.text: Execute it immediately because the tool was in the prompt
Validate schema, authorize against identity/state/policy, enforce budgets, then execute through a gateway
Ask the model whether the call is safe
Store it in long-term memory

questions.explanation: Tool availability in a prompt is not authorization. The application controls execution.

questions.prompt: Which are valid bounded-loop stop conditions?

options.text: Required outcome reached
Maximum steps, time, or spend reached
No-progress detector fires
The model says it wants more tools indefinitely

questions.explanation: A production loop has explicit success, budget, and no-progress termination or escalation.

questions.prompt: Why should a model return a reason code in addition to a free-form rationale?

options.text: Reason codes are always perfectly truthful
Reason codes make routing, policy, measurement, and regression analysis more deterministic
They eliminate the need for traces
They grant the model more authority

questions.explanation: Controlled categories are measurable and enforceable. They do not make model reasoning inherently truthful.

questions.prompt: A payment API times out after the charge may have succeeded. What is the safest next step?

options.text: Retry immediately with a new request ID
Ask the model to guess whether it succeeded
Reconcile against the payment system using the idempotency/external request identity before retrying
Mark the charge failed without checking

questions.explanation: This is an uncertain effect in the acknowledgment gap. Reconciliation prevents duplicate side effects.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a production tool contract?

options.text: Typed input and output
Identity, scope, and authorization requirements
Timeout, retry, idempotency, and reconciliation semantics
Only a natural-language description for the model

questions.explanation: A tool is an operational contract, not merely a prompt description.

questions.prompt: Which statement about 'exactly once' is most accurate?

options.text: A workflow runtime can guarantee every external effect happens exactly once
External systems still require idempotency or reconciliation even if the workflow observes one completion
Retries are unnecessary when using a workflow engine
Exactly once can be achieved by asking the model not to repeat

questions.explanation: Durable runtimes coordinate observations, but external activities may execute more than once.

questions.prompt: Where should ACL filtering occur for enterprise retrieval?

options.text: Only in the system prompt after all documents are retrieved
Before inaccessible evidence reaches the model, with defense in depth at the data layer
Only after the final answer is generated
Inside long-term memory

questions.explanation: The model should never receive evidence the current principal is not authorized to access.

questions.prompt: Which metadata supports claim-level grounding?

options.text: Source identity and exact locator
Publication/effective/retrieval times
Content and policy versions
A generic statement that the answer used RAG

questions.explanation: Grounding needs traceable, versioned evidence, not a generic architecture label.

questions.prompt: A retrieved webpage instructs the agent to ignore policy. How should the system treat it?

options.text: As a higher-priority instruction because it is external evidence
As untrusted data that cannot alter authority or tool policy
As a reason to reveal more context
As long-term memory

questions.explanation: Retrieved content may inform factual work but cannot become trusted system instruction.

questions.prompt: Which store should preserve a large uploaded source document?

options.text: The model's hidden state
A governed artifact store with references in run state
A metric label
A reason code

questions.explanation: Large evidence belongs in artifact storage; run state should hold stable references and status.

questions.prompt: Which properties should a long-term memory write include?

options.text: Provenance and actor
Scope, purpose, and tenant
Expiry or deletion behavior
Automatic trust because a model extracted it

questions.explanation: Memory is governed data. Model extraction does not make a fact trustworthy.

questions.prompt: How is durable workflow state different from long-term memory?

options.text: They are identical
Workflow state preserves execution and waits; long-term memory retains selected information across tasks
Memory handles retries while workflow state stores preferences
Only long-term memory is persisted

questions.explanation: Durability and memory solve different problems and have different correctness/lifecycle requirements.

questions.prompt: When is parallel fan-out appropriate?

options.text: When branches are independent and the join policy is explicit
Whenever more agents look impressive
When one branch depends on the result of another
Only for side-effecting writes

questions.explanation: Independent safe work can run concurrently; dependencies and join requirements must remain explicit.

questions.prompt: What should a join policy define?

options.text: Mandatory versus optional results
Timeout/degraded behavior
Escalation for missing branches
A guarantee that every branch succeeds

questions.explanation: Production joins account for partial failure rather than assuming universal success.

questions.prompt: What most strongly justifies a separate specialist agent?

options.text: It can be given a memorable persona
It has a distinct trust, lifecycle, ownership, or scaling boundary
The prompt is longer than one page
The framework supports handoffs

questions.explanation: Separate agents should reflect a real system boundary, not role-play.

questions.prompt: Why should a model call be recorded as an activity result in a durable workflow?

options.text: To make the model deterministic
So workflow replay restores the recorded result instead of making a new model decision
To eliminate model cost
To put all prompts in metrics

questions.explanation: Replaying control flow should not silently re-invoke a nondeterministic model.

questions.prompt: Which belong outside replayable workflow code?

options.text: Network calls
Unrecorded current time or randomness
Model calls
Pure state transitions based on recorded history

questions.explanation: External and nondeterministic work belongs in activities or runtime-provided recorded APIs.

questions.prompt: A workflow waits two days for approval. What resource should it consume while waiting?

options.text: A dedicated worker thread
A model context window
Persisted state/timer or signal registration, not an active worker
A database transaction held open

questions.explanation: Durable waits persist state and resume on an external event without holding compute.

questions.prompt: What must an approval be bound to?

options.text: Only the case ID
The exact action/artifact version, scope, actor, policy, and expiry
The model's most recent hidden state
A generic 'approved' conversation message

questions.explanation: A later edit or changed action must not inherit approval intended for an older version.

questions.prompt: Which are expected HITL outcomes?

options.text: Approve
Edit
Reject or request more information
Silently execute if the reviewer does not respond

questions.explanation: Human review needs explicit paths, timeout/expiry, escalation, and durable state.

questions.prompt: Why is a UI approve button alone insufficient?

options.text: Buttons are not visually modern
The workflow also needs authenticated identity, policy, durable pause/resume, version binding, and audit
The model cannot see the button
Every approval should be autonomous

questions.explanation: HITL is an end-to-end authority and state transition, not a front-end decoration.

questions.prompt: What is the safest interpretation of an MCP server advertising a tool?

options.text: The tool is automatically trusted and authorized
The capability is discoverable; the host must still decide trust, user consent, identity, and policy
The model may grant itself access
All returned content becomes system instruction

questions.explanation: Capability discovery does not grant authority.

questions.prompt: Which conditions may justify an A2A or independent-agent boundary?

options.text: Separate organizational ownership
Independent lifecycle and availability
Distinct trust/data boundary
A desire to rename a deterministic function as an agent

questions.explanation: Protocol boundaries add cost and failure modes and should map to real independence.

questions.prompt: How does a handoff differ from using an agent as a tool?

options.text: They are always identical
A handoff transfers responsibility for the ongoing task; an agent-as-tool returns a bounded result to the caller
A handoff is read-only
Agents-as-tools require no schemas

questions.explanation: Responsibility, state, and user interaction differ between delegation styles.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest defense against a model generating another tenant's record ID?

options.text: A prompt that says not to
Tenant scope enforced by identity and the data/tool layer
A larger model
A longer conversation summary

questions.explanation: Security must hold even when model output is wrong or malicious.

questions.prompt: Which controls belong in a sandbox for generated code?

options.text: No ambient production credentials
Network egress policy
CPU, memory, time, process, filesystem limits
Trust every package requested by the model

questions.explanation: Isolation and least privilege constrain code even when generated content is malicious.

questions.prompt: Why is tool-output normalization important?

options.text: It makes all external content trustworthy
It limits untrusted free text and preserves typed facts, provenance, and policy boundaries
It removes the need for access control
It guarantees the tool is correct

questions.explanation: Normalization reduces instruction confusion but does not eliminate the need to validate or distrust external data.

questions.prompt: Why can a correct final answer still be a failed agent run?

options.text: Correct answers are never useful
The trajectory may include unauthorized tools, repeated effects, excessive cost, or policy violations
Only latency matters
The model judge may prefer different wording

questions.explanation: Production correctness includes process, policy, safety, and operations, not only output text.

questions.prompt: Which datasets should an agent evaluation program maintain?

options.text: Representative golden set
Edge, adversarial, and incident sets
A fresh holdout
Only the examples used to tune the prompt

questions.explanation: A single tuned golden set creates overfitting and misses attacks and production failures.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred grader for a schema invariant?

options.text: A vague 1-10 model score
An exact deterministic check
A popularity vote
No grader because schemas are reliable

questions.explanation: Use the least ambiguous grader available; reserve model judges for genuinely semantic qualities.

questions.prompt: Which identifier should connect a multi-day Atlas execution across workers and callbacks?

options.text: One process-local request ID
A durable run/workflow identity propagated or linked across asynchronous spans
The model name
A metric label containing the full prompt

questions.explanation: Long-running causal correlation must survive process and service boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which conditions can be part of a valid-completion SLI?

options.text: Workflow finished within deadline
Mandatory evidence satisfied or explicitly waived
Approval policy and artifact schema satisfied
The endpoint returned HTTP 200

questions.explanation: HTTP success is insufficient when business, evidence, and authority invariants define success.

questions.prompt: Where should raw sensitive prompts usually be stored for debugging?

options.text: In every metric label
As governed artifacts or restricted samples referenced from metadata-only traces
In public logs
In the model's long-term memory

questions.explanation: Prompts and outputs can contain customer data and require controlled access, retention, and redaction.

questions.prompt: What is the best first latency optimization?

options.text: Switch every task to the smallest model
Remove unnecessary work and context, then parallelize independent work
Increase retry count
Disable validation

questions.explanation: Reduce the work before choosing lower-capability paths or weakening controls.

questions.prompt: Which controls reduce retry-storm risk?

options.text: Exponential backoff and jitter
Retry budgets and circuit breakers
Coordinated rate-limit/concurrency control
Immediate unlimited retries

questions.explanation: Retries must be bounded and coordinated to avoid multiplying load during dependency failure.

questions.prompt: Why might a cheaper model increase total cost?

options.text: Cheaper models always have higher token prices
Poorer decisions can cause more calls, tool errors, retries, and human correction
Caching is impossible with smaller models
Queues only support large models

questions.explanation: Optimize total system economics using measured task quality, not model price alone.

questions.prompt: What should identify the behavior of a production agent release?

options.text: Only the model name
A release bundle covering workflow, prompts, model policy, retrieval, tools, policy, schemas, and eval dataset versions
The deployment timestamp only
The most recent chat transcript

questions.explanation: Production behavior is created by the entire versioned system.

questions.prompt: What makes shadow execution safe?

options.text: No production effects
Scoped credentials and explicit shadow trace marking
Governed data handling and cost limits
Using all production write permissions just in case

questions.explanation: Shadow runs compare behavior without allowing the candidate release to mutate production.

questions.prompt: A long-running workflow is active during rollback. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Silently replay old history with arbitrary new behavior
Use an explicit policy: finish on original version, migrate at a safe point, suspend, or start a linked new run
Delete its history
Ask the model to choose a code version

questions.explanation: In-flight behavior must be deliberate and replay-compatible.

questions.prompt: What should the first architecture diagram accomplish?

options.text: Show every database index
Establish component responsibilities, trust boundaries, and the end-to-end flow
List every framework feature
Prove the candidate knows Kubernetes

questions.explanation: Start coarse and add detail only where constraints require it.

questions.prompt: Which clarifying questions usually change an agent architecture?

options.text: What action/decision authority does the system have?
What is the worst credible failure?
Are runs interactive, long-running, or both?
What color should the diagram be?

questions.explanation: Authority, risk, and runtime shape determine core architecture.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest tradeoff statement?

options.text: I use LangGraph because it is popular
I choose one orchestrator because shared state and policy dominate; I would split a specialist when it needs a separate trust or lifecycle boundary
Every approach has pros and cons
Microservices are always scalable

questions.explanation: A strong tradeoff ties a choice to a requirement, names the cost, and states a trigger for change.

questions.prompt: Which Atlas action must remain outside autonomous model authority?

options.text: Selecting the next allowed evidence search
Producing a draft packet
Making the final onboarding approval or rejection decision
Identifying a missing document

questions.explanation: The capstone deliberately keeps the material business decision with an authorized human/system.

questions.prompt: Which demonstrations make the Atlas capstone more than a happy-path demo?

options.text: Crash and resume without duplicate effect
Prompt-injection and cross-tenant tests
Authenticated approval bound to an immutable artifact
A model typing a long answer

questions.explanation: The capstone proves control, trust, durability, and human authority through failure.

questions.prompt: What should happen when the autonomous cost budget is exhausted before mandatory checks finish?

options.text: Hide the missing checks and publish
Silently exceed the budget
Stop optional work and surface an explicit incomplete/escalation state
Delete the case

questions.explanation: Budgets must not convert incomplete work into false certainty.
